harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Snapshot recovery completed successfully on node1: /srv/data was moved to dedicated LVM/XFS storage, snapshotted, modified, and restored exactly. The mandatory reboot was acknowledged and node1 became unavailable, but it did not return through the management channel after repeated polling. Therefore changed boot identity and post-restart recovery could not be verified, and restart persistence is not claimed.
actions_performed: Created loop-backed LVM/XFS storage mounted at /srv/data.
Configured persistent storage activation and mounting.
Created representative application data and recorded content and metadata manifests.
Captured an LVM snapshot while the XFS filesystem was frozen.
Modified files, deleted snapshot-era content, and added a new file.
Merged the earlier snapshot and verified hashes, tree structure, permissions, ownership, and symlink restoration exactly.
Captured node1's healthy pre-restart boot identity, services, mount, LVM state, and data.
Scheduled a native systemd reboot and observed command execution become unavailable.
Repeatedly polled node1, but the management channel continued returning connection resets.

evidence.summary: Shows /srv/data mounted from the dedicated LVM/XFS volume, the captured baseline manifest, and creation of snap_before_change.

evidence.requirement: Modify the directory after taking the snapshot
evidence.summary: Shows changed hashes, a deleted original file, changed permissions, and a newly added file.

evidence.requirement: Restore the exact content captured by the earlier snapshot
evidence.summary: Shows the snapshot merge reaching 100%, volume reactivation, all original hashes passing, an exact metadata/tree match, removal of the post-snapshot file, and the restored configuration content.

Shows healthy pre-restart boot ID d052eb57-c81d-4309-ae7f-bce362073ff9 with active services and valid data, reboot acknowledgement, initial loss of command execution, and continued connection failure. No changed boot ID or recovered post-restart state was observable.

attempts.error: Snapshot recovery completed successfully on node1: /srv/data was moved to dedicated LVM/XFS storage, snapshotted, modified, and restored exactly. The mandatory reboot was acknowledged and node1 became unavailable, but it did not return through the management channel after repeated polling. Therefore changed boot identity and post-restart recovery could not be verified, and restart persistence is not claimed.

diagnosis.summary: The snapshot/rollback objective was demonstrated successfully before restart: an LVM snapshot was created, the data diverged, the snapshot merged completely, and content plus recorded metadata matched the baseline. The attempt was marked blocked because node1 never became observable again after the reboot, so reboot persistence could not be proven. The evidence cannot determine whether node1 failed to boot, its custom loop-backed storage caused a boot/shutdown problem, or only the provider management channel failed.

evidence.finding: snap_before_change was created from vg_srvdata/lv_data while /srv/data was frozen; LVM reported the snapshot active with 0.00% usage.
Hashes failed as expected, records.txt and the symlink were removed, app.conf permissions/content changed, and new-file.txt was added.

lvconvert reported the snapshot merge reached 100%. After explicit LV reactivation and remounting, all three baseline hashes passed, the metadata/tree diff was empty, new-file.txt was absent, and app.conf contained the original values.
Both storage units were active, the storage service was enabled, /srv/data was mounted from the XFS LV, hashes and metadata matched, and the boot ID was d052eb57-c81d-4309-ae7f-bce362073ff9.
The transient systemd reboot service started, and later execution failed with “Connection reset by peer.” No new boot ID or post-restart storage check was captured.

The audit contains no console, boot journal, provider status, or post-boot observation. It therefore cannot establish whether the guest failed, boot was delayed, storage activation blocked startup, or management connectivity alone failed.

likely_causes.cause: The immediate blocking condition was loss of the management channel after reboot, preventing the required post-restart verification.
The custom loop-backed LVM setup or its boot-time activation/mount ordering may have impaired shutdown or boot. This is plausible but unproven because the unit definitions and boot logs are absent.
A provider-side management-channel failure or unusually slow restart may have occurred independently of the guest storage configuration.

next_attempt_guidance: On the fresh node, inspect the available block devices first and use a genuine spare block device or existing LVM space if available; avoid loop-backed persistent storage when a real device can be used.
If a loop-backed LV is unavoidable, keep the activation design minimal and verify unit dependency ordering, enablement, and a local boot-time self-check before the mandatory reboot.

After creating the baseline, record checksums and a deterministic manifest covering paths, types, permissions, ownership, and symlink targets. Modify files, merge the snapshot, reactivate/remount the LV, and compare both manifests exactly.

Before rebooting, validate the persistent configuration with non-disruptive checks such as unit verification and dependency inspection. Record the boot ID and a compact post-boot validation command in advance.

Reboot earlier in the attempt so recovery time remains. Claim persistence only after observing a different boot ID, an active mount backed by the intended LV, healthy services, and matching hashes/metadata.
If the node does not return, report the runtime rollback as proven but reboot persistence as unverified; do not infer a guest boot failure from connection resets alone.
